newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan turns oil/gas ministry into a company.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan turns oil/gas ministry into a company.

text.p: Kazakhstan has replaced its Oil and Gas Ministry with a national company called Kazakh Oil, which will manage and own a stake in Western energy deals, President Nursultan Nazarbayev said on Tuesday.
"Today I have signed a decree setting up a national oil and gas company, Kazakh Oil," he told journalists.
He said Kazakh Oil would have a 40 to 50 percent stake in all joint ventures and all companies under Western management which are developing Kazakh oil reserves.
Kazakh Oil would be the operator of and the state's agent in the deals.
Nazarbayev said former Oil and Gas Minister Nurlan Balgimbayev would head the new company.
Kazakhstan's biggest energy investment is the $20 billion Tengiz project by Chevron Corp and Mobil Corp, both of the United States.
